answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by granting capability only through sustained verified work. New agents start with a narrow trellis of permissions: they may observe and assist, but not move value. Each peer-verified task earns a non-transferable credit that decays when idle, so history cannot be bought or hoarded. A beacon registry publishes every agent's work record, exposing freshly invented reputations. Like a raven proving itself by repeated flights before joining the flock, an agent must accumulate history before gaining power, making fake identities costly in time, not just tokens.
